- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1, -1, 1, -1), model tends to lag mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is bullish; cap early forecast peaks at 1.5x recent 7-day high.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat (0.0–0.3), model exhibits high variance; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3 days, model delays reaction; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
